sentences.text: Neutral Citation No. - 2023:AHC:112004 Court No. - 82 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 5107 of 2023 Applicant :- Omprakash Sahani

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Dheeraj Kumar Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mukesh Kumar Pandey Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned counsel for the opposite party alongwith learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.216 of 2016, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., Police Station Ramkola,
District Kushinagar, during the pendency of trial.
It is submitted that in this case applicant is innocent and has committed no offence.
Further submitted that after investigation charge sheet has been filed in the present case but on account of non-information about the process he could not appear before the learned court.

It is also submitted that he never got forged caste certificate issued by the authorities but allegation in this regard is Omprakash Sahani vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34031836/
1 totally false.

sentences.text: Now applicant is ready to face the trial but is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that the allegation as made in the F.I.R. was enquired into by the authorities in which it was found to be prima facie established on the basis of material collected during investigation.

It is further urged that there are 16 cases as criminal history against the applicant including Gunda Act and Gangster Act and applicant is also not making cooperation with the trial, therefore, he cannot be said to be entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, the allegation against the applicant and long criminal history of 16 cases, there appears no ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of this applicant.
Hence, the anticipatory bail application is, hereby, rejected.

However, as per the submission of learned counsel for the applicant, in case applicant appears and moves bail application before the learned court concerned within a period of six weeks, the same shall be decided by it as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 22.5.2023 Ashok Gupta  Omprakash Sahani vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34031836/
